narrative: Brentford sit 7th and are pushing for a Europa League spot in what would be a remarkable season despite a raft of long-term absentees. For Wolves — bottom of the table with just 3 wins all season — this is as close to a must-win as a 20th-placed side gets with 8 games left.

Michael Carrick's United arrive at the Vitality in red-hot form — 5 wins in his first 6 league games after the Amorim sacking — and will be desperate to keep pace with Aston Villa in the top-four race. Bournemouth (10th) are comfortable but have quietly won three of their last five, making this a trickier away day than the table suggests.
awayInjuries: Matthijs de Ligt (back — serious doubt, may miss rest of season)
managerNote: Michael Carrick (Man Utd) — appointed Jan 13, 2026. Won 5 of his first 6 PL games. Roberto De Zerbi linked for the permanent role but Carrick is building a strong case. Hojlund exit to Napoli (€50m) confirmed, freeing up summer funds.

narrative: Liverpool desperately need a response after Wolves stunned them at Molineux in GW30 — a result that leaves Arne Slot's side fighting just to hold onto a European spot, let alone top four. Brighton head into this in confident mood after back-to-back league wins, but Liverpool with a point to prove at the Amex is dangerous.
homeInjuries: Kaoru Mitoma (ankle — doubt, forced off vs Arsenal Mar 4)

narrative: Burnley are second-bottom with 4 wins all season and a goal difference of -34 — a trip to a mid-table Fulham side in decent form is a fixture they desperately need a result from. Fulham have been quietly consistent (12W-7D-11L) and a home win here could push them towards an outside Europa challenge.

Crystal Palace arrive fresh from a stunning 3-1 win at Tottenham last week, but face a very different proposition at the Etihad.

narrative: The Tyne-Wear derby returns to St James' Park for the first time since Sunderland's return to the top flight — an occasion drenched in local rivalry that transcends league positions. Newcastle (9th) need the points for a Europa push, while Sunderland's first taste of a Tyneside derby in years will be a defining moment for their promoted squad.

narrative: This is arguably the biggest six-pointer of the season — two clubs staring down the barrel of the drop meet in what could define both their fates. Igor Tudor's Spurs are winless in 5 since his appointment, while Forest's Vítor Pereira is similarly yet to find a league win; one of them must blink first.
